sample_unit: patients with lymph node metastases (whole-slide images); plus 1012 tumor-negative slides for false-positive alerts

links.outcome: Sensitivity of AI tools on tumor types beyond their intended use
links.effect: Both tools showed excellent sensitivity for macrometastases across tumor types, including beyond intended use. DPL had slightly higher sensitivity for micrometastases and isolated tumor cells than VMD, particularly in lung cancer and melanoma.
links.quote: Our findings suggest that a single AI tool may be suitable for LN metastasis detection across multiple tumor types, even beyond its intended use.

links.outcome: False-positive alert rates in tumor-negative slides
links.effect: FPA rates were substantial for both tools; VMD generally produced more alerts, especially in lung and breast cancer. High FPA rates, even in lung cancer within DPL's intended use, may limit practical use.
links.quote: FPA rates were substantial for both tools, with VMD generally producing more alerts, especially in lung and breast cancer.

unlisted_practices: Multipurpose validation of AI tools beyond certified intended use across tumor types to improve business case

screen.reason: Evaluates the diagnostic performance and false positive rates of CE-IVD certified pathology AI tools when deployed outside their certified intended use indications across multiple cancer types.

primary.practice: off-label multi-cancer validation beyond intended use
